issue: Must a criminal defendant's claim that was never presented to the district court be reviewed only for plain error under Rule 52(b), or may the appellate court review it de novo because a postruling exception is unnecessary under Rule 51(a)?
provision: Fed. R. Crim. P. 51(b); Fed. R. Crim. P. 52(b)

sides.position: Claims never presented to the district court are reviewed only for plain error under Rule 52(b); Rule 51(a) does not excuse the contemporaneous-objection requirement of Rule 51(b).
cases: United States v. Stapleton, No. 25-2201 (7th Cir. 2026)

sides.position: Claims never presented to the district court may be reviewed de novo because Rule 51(a) makes a postruling exception unnecessary.
cases: Circuit decisions the Stapleton opinion describes as having applied de novo review to unpreserved claims (not named in the excerpt)

this_court: The Seventh Circuit adopts the plain-error position and rejects its own prior practice of de novo review of claims never presented.
quote: They are also in considerable tension with Supreme Court precedent and have created a lopsided circuit split.
cite: United States v. Jermaine Stapleton, No. 25-2201 (7th Cir. 2026)
